narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story and introduces each speech.

eliu.name: Eliu
eliu.note: Son of Barachel the Buzite; the angry young bystander who speaks after the three friends fall silent.

1.t: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he seemed just to himself.

2.t: And Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite of the kindred of Ram, was angry and was moved to indignation: now he was angry against Job, because he said he was just before God.

3.t: And he was angry with his friends, because they had not found a reasonable answer, but only had condemned Job.

4.t: So Eliu waited while Job was speaking because they were his elders that were speaking.

5.t: But when he saw that the three were not able to answer, he was exceedingly angry.

6.t: Then Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, and said:
I am younger in days, and you are more ancient, therefore hanging down my head, I was afraid to shew you my opinion.

7.t: For I hoped that greater age would speak, and that a multitude of years would teach wisdom.

8.t: But, as I see, there is a spirit in men, and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth understanding.

9.t: They that are aged are not the wise men, neither do the ancients understand judgment.

10.t: Therefore I will speak: Hearken to me, I also will shew you my wisdom.

11.t: For I have waited for your words, I have given ear to your wisdom, as long as you were disputing in words.

12.t: And as long as I thought you said some thing, I considered: but, as I see, there is none of you that can convince Job, and answer his words.

13.t: Lest you should say: We have found wisdom, God hath cast him down, not man.

14.t: He hath spoken nothing to me, and I will not answer him according to your words.

15.t: They were afraid, and answered no more, and they left off speaking.
15.q: Third-person remark on the friends' silence; read as Eliu's aside within his speech, not narration

16.t: Therefore because I have waited, and they have not spoken: they stood, and answered no more:
16.q: 'they stood, and answered no more' kept with Eliu as part of his own sentence, not narration

17.t: I also will answer my part, and will shew my knowledge.

18.t: For I am full of matter to speak of, and the spirit of my bowels straiteneth me.

19.t: Behold, my belly is as new wine which wanteth vent, which bursteth the new vessels.

20.t: I will speak and take breath a little: I will open my lips, and will answer.

21.t: I will not accept the person of man, and I will not level God with man.

22.t: For I know not how long I shall continue, and whether after a while my Maker may take me away.
